W2_20_WIDENING_ADJUDICATION.why_this_is_decided_without_resolving_th: There are two defensible readings of whether an UNREGISTERED but DECLARED grant is an 'existing grant' for the purposes of the v1.0.15 prohibition. Reading one: the declaration IS the grant, because v1.0.15 itself calls the addendum's protected_grant object 'source_of_truth' and treats the registry as its mechanical projection - so W2-20 exists and amending it is prohibited outright. Reading two: 'existing' attaches at registration, and W2-20's measured zero registry presence means no live object is being mutated. THE SEPARATE-GRANT ROUTE IS CORRECT UNDER BOTH READINGS, so the adjudication does not depend on resolving the ambiguity, and none is asserted. This is deliberately the more conservative of the two available routes and the more expensive one in registry cardinality; it was chosen against the convenient answer.
